findings.title: VIEW permission on all groups grants manage rights to all groups
findings.body: canManage() checks hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). A caller who only has the global Groups view scope is therefore treated as having manage rights. requireManage() is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() and group update/delete flows, so this allows users with view-only permission to create or modify groups. The check should require AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE only.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group model IDs and may not enumerate per-group resources
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates resources returned by findByType and passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission(), then adds that ID to the returned set. The returned set is used as GroupModel IDs for the UserModel.GROUPS search attribute in UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource. However, group permission resources are created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() with the group model ID as the resource name and a separate generated authorization resource UUID as the resource ID; getId() is not the group ID. In addition, those per-group resources are not created with type Groups, so findByType may not find them. The result is that user search/count filtering by viewable groups receives invalid or empty group IDs and can return wrong results. The code should use groupResource.getName() and ensure resources are actually typed and enumerable.

findings.title: Existing admin permissions clients are not migrated with the new Groups resource type and scopes
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null. Realms that already initialized the V2 admin permissions schema before this change will therefore not get the new Groups resource type or the new group scopes. Later, GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() can call getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE), receive null, and then call policyStore.findByResource(server, resource), causing an NPE; alternatively, Groups permissions cannot be configured or enforced for those realms. Initialization should create the missing Groups resource/scopes for existing admin permission clients.
